name: Utah

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (Utah Code 58-87)

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers endorsement contracts (Utah Code 58-87-102), and Utah's NIL law uses the same agent definition (53H-6-201).
summary: Get licensed by DOPL. $510. Renews September 30 of even years.
contract_warning:
Warning to student athlete
If you sign this contract:
(1) You may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport;
(2) If you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and
(3) You may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student athlete in your sport.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: This also applies before you have someone else contact them. If the athlete reached out first, tell them within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Say you're registered in Utah and list your other states. Add your pay and how it's figured, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the state's warning in bold next to the athlete's signature
steps.detail: Use the exact words in the warning box.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. A parent or guardian signs if the athlete is a minor.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy of the contract and the signed warning when they sign
Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell them too.

steps.text: Let the athlete cancel in writing within 14 days
steps.detail: They can't give up this right. If they cancel, they owe you nothing.

steps.text: If you signed before the athlete enrolled, tell the new school's athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The clock starts when you knew or should have known they enrolled.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: State law (58-87-401) and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of clients, every contract, and what you spent recruiting each athlete.

steps.text: Never give false info to get an athlete to sign
steps.detail: Don't contact athletes until you're licensed. Don't have anyone do these things for you.

steps.text: If you give an athlete anything that could cost their eligibility, tell the athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The athlete must also say in writing that they know it could cost their eligibility. Without both, the gift breaks the law.
Every even year. The next renewal is Sept 30, 2028.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: DOPL sets the fee, not the statute (58-87-206). The $510 is from DOPL's fee schedule, updated June 30, 2026. It can change each July.
